verdicts.what_is_true_en: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed near the Moon's south pole on August 23, 2023, making it the first country to achieve this.
verdicts.reasoning_en: Multiple credible sources, including the space agency NASA (ws-5) and various news outlets (ws-2, ws-7), confirm that India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed near the Moon's south pole on August 23, 2023. The evidence consistently states that this made India the first country to achieve a soft landing in this region. While some fact-checks (fc-1, fc-2, fc-3) debunked fake footage related to the event, they do not contradict the fact that the landing itself occurred.

verdicts.label: TRUE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: With the successful landing of Chandrayaan-3 in August 2023, India became the fourth country to achieve a soft landing on the Moon, after the United States, the former Soviet Union, and China.
verdicts.reasoning_en: Numerous sources confirm that India's successful lunar landing made it the fourth country to achieve this feat. The evidence consistently lists the other three countries as the United States, the former Soviet Union, and China. One source (ws-13) adds that Japan became the fifth country to do so in January 2024, which further solidifies India's position as the fourth.

verdicts.label: TRUE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: The Vikram lander of India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully touched down on the Moon at 18:04 Indian Standard Time (IST) on August 23, 2023, which is equivalent to 12:34 GMT.
verdicts.reasoning_en: Multiple credible news and science-focused sources confirm the exact time of the Chandrayaan-3 landing. The evidence consistently states the touchdown occurred at 18:04 Indian Standard Time (IST) on August 23, 2023. Several sources also provide the corresponding time in GMT as 12:34, confirming all parts of the claim.
